value: rarely from hen to chick through the egg
can also enter through broken skin on the feet or legs
swelling or bleeding around the joints
gut, respiratory or nervous system signs in some cases
stunted growth and small body size (runting-stunting syndrome)
in young broilers: bruising under the skin and in muscle with poor growth (blue wing disease)

mortality.value: Blue wing disease in young broilers has an average death rate of about 10%

diagnosis.value: Signs alone give only a suspected diagnosis; confirming it needs lab tests such as virus isolation, complement fixation, ELISA, immunodiffusion or tissue examination after death

value: vaccination of breeder hens so chicks get protection through maternal antibodies

summary.value: Avian orthoreovirus is found worldwide in poultry flocks and mainly causes joint disease and lameness, along with runting-stunting problems in young birds. It is not caught by people, spreads mostly through droppings, and vaccination of breeding flocks is the main way to protect chicks.
